issues.description: Malformed XML raises ElementTree.ParseError instead of producing a structured warning, despite the documented warning-never-raises contract.
XML ingest uses stdlib ElementTree directly on input files without hardened parsing or size/entity protections.
Non-finite scores such as NaN pass through unclamped and can crash SQLite inserts or poison reports.
Format B assumes metrics is dict-like; a non-empty non-dict metrics value raises AttributeError instead of a malformed-row warning.
Ingest only upserts current records and never deletes rows removed from input files, so the database can retain stale results.
Format A accepts empty run_id, model, or task values, allowing blank keys and meaningless canonical records.
Format B coerces missing or null required fields into strings like 'None' or empty task/model values instead of rejecting malformed records.
Format C accepts missing run id, model, and task text, which can create blank-key rows and overwrite unrelated malformed runs.
Format A reads the entire CSV file into memory instead of streaming rows, which is risky for large evaluation exports.
Format B reads the entire JSONL file into memory instead of streaming line by line.
Format A parses CSV one physical line at a time, so valid quoted multiline CSV fields are not supported.
The ingest CLI lets parser and database exceptions escape as tracebacks instead of returning a controlled error.
Package metadata is minimal and does not declare README, license, authors, or a test/dev dependency extra for pytest.
There is no linting, formatting, typing, coverage, or CI configuration despite data-quality code relying on strict edge-case behavior.
Pipeline tests cover generated fixtures well but omit malformed XML, malformed object shapes, non-finite scores, stale-row deletion, and large-file behavior.
